Performance under feature noise, input corruption, induced missingness and reduced training data, and transfer across time periods and across disjoint instrument sets.
Where does the detector stop being reliable, and does it transfer beyond the instruments and period it was fitted on?

Five axes execute: additive noise, value dropout, stale feed, outlier injection and per-block blackout on the evaluation inputs; a symbol-level training-size curve; expanding-window transfer forward in time; and transfer to disjoint tickers. The model is fitted once on clean data for the input-degradation axis, because refitting on corrupted data measures whether the learner adapts, which is an easier and different question than what a deployed model does when its feed degrades. Training subsampling drops whole symbols rather than random rows: rows from one instrument are serially dependent, so row-level dropping leaves nearly every instrument represented and understates how much the model depends on breadth. The frozen holdout is never read -- assert_no_holdout() raises on any frame carrying holdout rows and every fit passes through it. Cross-dataset transfer remains BLOCKED and is reported as such, because only one dataset exists. Adversarial robustness is NOT RUN: every corruption here is random, and an adversarial claim needs a threat model.

One perturbation condition, run now: the model is fitted on clean data and scored on degraded inputs. Fitting once is the point — refitting on corrupted data asks whether the learner adapts, which is not what a degraded feed does to a deployed model.

Repeat the stochastic parts of the pipeline across seeds and report mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum and 95% confidence interval, then apply the existing cluster bootstrap, paired permutation, Benjamini-Hochberg correction and power analysis to the repeated measurements.
How much of the reported difference between arms is seed variance rather than signal?

Every ablation arm is refitted across a declared seed ladder and the repeated measurements are handed to the machinery that already existed: cluster bootstrap, paired sign-flip permutation and Benjamini-Hochberg. Two sources of variation are kept apart, because conflating them is how a seed study overstates its own precision -- spread across seeds on one fixed evaluation set is seed variance, and the cluster bootstrap interval within one run is sampling variance of the evaluation set. A pooled seed noise floor is reported, and an arm difference smaller than that floor is recorded as not established however it looked in a single run. Differences that dissolve are listed alongside the ones that survive rather than filtered out. Validation only: repeating a measurement on the frozen holdout across ten seeds would be ten looks at the data the freeze exists to protect.
